description.short: A keeper’s cottage stands above a stream crossed by a fallen willow. Behind it are kennels; inside hang the tools of a living learnt through years of walking, watching and handling animals. Richard Jefferies follows that work into woods, fields and neighbouring villages, where a broken twig or a disturbed rabbit hole may carry news.
description.long:
A keeper’s cottage stands above a stream crossed by a fallen willow. Behind it are kennels; inside hang the tools of a living learnt through years of walking, watching and handling animals. Richard Jefferies follows that work into woods, fields and neighbouring villages, where a broken twig or a disturbed rabbit hole may carry news.

The Gamekeeper at Home brings natural history into the daily business of an estate. Birds must be reared, dogs trained, trees watched and household resources put to use. The keeper knows his ground through repeated attention, while the writer beside him finds time to listen at a burrow or follow an animal beyond the demands of the day’s work. Employment, family life and the knowledge passed between generations give these country sketches their human setting.

The English text of 1878 is accompanied by Charles Whymper’s drawings from the illustrated edition of 1880, with an account of the author, an afterword and a glossary.

AMBER SERIES · AETERNUS
